transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Russia fired a ballistic missile on the hometown
of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The attack killed a seven-year-old boy
and a 20-year-old paramedic.
More than 50 others were injured.
NPR's owner Beardsley reports from Kyiv.
The attack targeted the densely-populated downtown area
of the southern town of Krivirikh.
Local official Alexander Vilkul called it
a tragic evening and night for our city
as Russian terrorists have launched
another series of criminal attacks.
Two ballistic missiles were launched
at an area near a popular restaurant,
followed by a swarm of Shahed-type drones
that struck first responders
in what's known as a double-tap strike.
The seven-year-old died in the hospital
after sustaining trauma to his head,
and a three- and four-year-old were among the wounded.
Meanwhile, in a call to European leaders
after his meeting with Russia's president in China Thursday,
President Trump told them Vladimir Putin
is serious about negotiating a peace deal.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Kyiv.
- The war in Ukraine was high on the agenda
at this week's Economic Summit in Asia,
where both President Trump and Russian president
Vladimir Putin attended.
NPR's Franco Ordonez says reporters repeatedly press Trump
on where the U.S. stands with Moscow.
- I mean, Trump was asked today if Putin,
who he called his friend, was also America's friend.
You know, he really couldn't answer that,
but he did continue to make the case
that his relationship with Putin
would reap benefits for America,
though we haven't really seen that yet.
You know, the war in Ukraine continues to rage on,
but we are seeing allies start to build alliances
with other nations as, you know,
confidence in the U.S. falters,
and they look to reduce their dependence on the U.S.
- NPR's Franco Ordonez.
Officials in New York City have released a plan
to close the jail complex on Rikers Island.
NPR's Meg Anderson reports the facility has been plagued
with reports of excessive force,
rampant sexual assault, and high rates of violence for years.
- The question of what to do with Rikers
has eluded New York City leaders for years.
- Now, New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani
has pledged to take on the jail's closure head-on.
- Today, we lead differently.
I am proud that New York City will close
Rikers Island once and for all.
- The city will build four smaller jails
across the city over the next six years,
which will require a dramatic reduction
in the city's jail population.
The city plan includes more diversion,
more services aimed at crime prevention,
strategies to speed up court cases
and better training and oversight for staff
aimed at not carrying the failures of Rikers
into the new jails.
Meg Anderson, NPR News.
- This is NPR News in Washington.
President Trump is threatening to hit U.S. tech companies
with what he calls a tremendous tax
if they build AI data centers overseas.
Speaking at the White House on Friday,
Trump offered no details on how the tax would work
and said he hadn't yet told his own officials
about the idea.
Trump says building more data centers at home
is critical to winning the AI race.
He urged communities to welcome the projects
and press tech companies for concessions.
Week-long funeral services for labor activists
Dolores Huerta have ended.
A public celebration of life took place last night
in Bakersfield, California.
Amare Alvarez from member station KVPR
reports she spent the last 30 years
of her life living there.
Members of Huerta's family and state leaders
spoke about her legacy at her final goodbye.
California's Democratic governor-elect,
Javier Becerra, highlighted her fight for farm worker rights.
- There's never been a day in my life
without Dolores Huerta.
There was never a fight that I saw
that didn't include Dolores Huerta.
- Former President Bill Clinton and actress Jane Fonda
appeared in video messages.
This event kept off a week of services
that started with Huerta laying in honor
in the state capitol.
By the end of the night, everyone was on their feet
dancing to the Mexican-American group Los Lobos.
For NPR, I'm Amare Alvarez in Bakersfield.
- And I'm Windsor Johnston,
and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
[BLANK_AUDIO]

topics.text: Russian ballistic missile strike on Zelensky's hometown Kryvyi Rih kills a seven-year-old boy and paramedic
Trump and Putin's Asia summit attendance and Trump's Ukraine war remarks draw reporter questions
New York City officials release plan to close Rikers Island jail complex with four smaller jails
Trump threatens tremendous tax on tech companies building AI data centers overseas
Week-long funeral services for labor activist Dolores Huerta conclude with celebration in Bakersfield, California
